observation_summary: The MonthDay class fails when performing arithmetic (plus/minus months/days) on leap dates (e.g., Feb 29). It throws an IllegalFieldValueException because it attempts to validate the day-of-month against a non-leap year range (1-28) during intermediate calculations, or incorrectly adjusts the date to Feb 28.
reasoning_summary: The issue is an algorithmic flaw in how date arithmetic is performed for partial dates like MonthDay. The code attempts to set the day-of-month field using a standard validation check (verifyValueBounds) that does not account for the context of leap years when performing additions or subtractions. This is a procedural logic error in the calculation method, not a missing guard or a simple assignment error.
evidence_used: org.joda.time.IllegalFieldValueException: Value 29 for dayOfMonth must be in the range [1,28]

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While the failure manifests as a failed check (IllegalFieldValueException), the root cause is the algorithmic approach to date arithmetic that fails to handle leap year context correctly, rather than a missing or incorrect guard condition.
The capability exists, but the implementation of the arithmetic logic is flawed for specific edge cases (leap years), which is a procedural/algorithmic issue.
